title: Acute Stress Disorder - BSV and Vocal Markers
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: BSV / Vocal

BSV / VOCAL SIGNALS: High Arousal (hypervigilance, startle, insomnia, irritability) immediately post-trauma. Low Valence (numbness, anhedonia, guilt). Dissociative symptoms may flatten affect and reduce prosodic variability. Voice often tremulous, breathy, or monotone during trauma narrative. Exaggerated startle may produce sudden pitch jumps.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "I keep seeing it when I close my eyes", "I feel like I'm watching myself from outside", "My heart races at every loud noise".

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: Low arousal or chronic low mood without recent trauma cue linkage argues against ASD. Absence of dissociative or intrusion symptoms in first month post-trauma reduces likelihood.

PROVENANCE: Observational studies of acute trauma response and acoustic affect in PTSD spectrum.
